copy.curiosityHook: When surveillance reveals Soviet missile installations just off American shores, how do leaders navigate the razor-thin margin between diplomacy and global conflict?
copy.description: In October 1962, American discovery of Soviet missile bases established in Cuba triggers a high-stakes Cold War standoff, plunging leadership into a fraught nuclear showdown directed by Roger Donaldson.
copy.vibeSummary: A tense, deliberate historical thriller with heavy emotional weight, demanding engaged focus across its 145-minute runtime.
copy.whyWatch: Roger Donaldson directs a gripping, history-rooted thriller where every calculated political move and diplomatic calculation carries the threat of catastrophic escalation.

allowedMaterial: Premise and setup of the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis
Discovery of Soviet missile bases in Cuba by Americans
Nuclear standoff between the United States and the USSR
Cold War political and diplomatic tension
Director Roger Donaldson and historical thriller genre details
excludedMaterial: Backchannel negotiations and final diplomatic deals
